title: Wasted time
body:
I’m tired of apps wasting my time with long questionnaires before letting me see the actual product. I spent more than five minutes filling out forms and still wasn’t able to try any real functionality before being asked to pay.

I understand the logic behind this flow: after investing time answering questions, users are probably more likely to pay rather than abandon the process. But understanding the strategy doesn’t make the experience any less frustrating.

I would much rather be allowed to try the core functionality first and then decide whether the product is worth paying for. This kind of onboarding feels like a conversion tactic rather than something designed for the user.

title: Die Idee ist super, die Umsetzung lässt zu wünschen übrig.
body:
Zu Anfang möchte ich sagen, ich habe die App nicht wirklich lange genutzt. Was mir direkt negativ aufgefallen ist, ist dass man am Anfang ein 10 minütiges Intro mit sensiblen Fragen beantwortet, danach gefühlte 30 mal die „Bewertungen“ gezeigt werden wie toll die App ist und man ganz am Ende zur Zahlung aufgefordert wird. Die 7 Tägige Testversion ist anscheinend nur für das Jahresabo, könnte ein bisschen besser kommuniziert sein, denn ich dachte die hat man immer und sofort wurden mir 14,99€ abgebucht :) Der Startbildschirm der App ist viel zu überladen für jemanden, der loskommen möchte von diesem ständigen Input (Social Media oder Gaming) erst recht, weil ich es vorher bei meinen Fragen angegeben habe. Da hier auch einige positive Bewertungen sind, gehe ich davon aus, dass es zum Teil mit meinem eigenen befinden zu tun hat. Abgesehen davon muss ich leider sagen, dass mich solche Apps mit diesem Vorgehen am Anfang sowieso abschrecken. Macht doch einfach mal 2 Wochen Testphase ohne Geld zu verlangen. Wenn ihr das richtig macht werdet ihr eure Kunden schon bei euch halten.

Edit: Der Kommentar des Unternehmens unter dieser Bewertung bestätigt meine Annahme. Das ist nicht hilfreich, das ist Werbung.

title: Kleine Kinderkrankheiten, sonst bisher sehr zufrieden
body:
Benutze die App seit 2 Wochen und bisher bin ich ganz zufrieden. Ich finde es cool, dass es a Solo Leveling angelehnt ist, aber viel alltagstauglicher. Ich habe das Gefühl es geht mir insgesamt besser und ich habe zwar seit 2 Wochen durchgehend mal mehr mal weniger Muskelkater, aber ich fühle mich insgesamt fitter und ich erkenne tatsächlich Fortschritte, sowohl körperlich als auch mental. 
Die App hat noch hier und da einpaar kleine Hänger und Baustellen. Manchmal zählt sie die Tage nicht richtig mit und man muss sich an-und abmelden, damit der Fortschritt wieder richtig angezeigt wird. Die Auswahl an Aktivitäten bzw. Ziele könnte breiter und gängiger sein (finde Tennis z.B. etwas random). Und wenn man schon das Geschlecht angeben kann, könnte der Plan auch etwas besser drauf zugeschnitten sein, v.a. an der Periode (die Leistungsfähigkeit ist sehr von ihr abhängig). Einpaar andere Punkte gibt es auch noch, aber insgesamt finde ich die App ganz cool. Ich finde es auch gut, dass man den “Hard-Modus” manuell wählen kann und er einem vom Programm selbst vorgeschlagen wird, wenn man gut mit den Aufgaben voran kommt. Auch die kleinen Level-Ups sind immer wieder motivierend. Ich bin gespannt wie ich die nächsten Tage und Wochen mit der App zurecht komme, aber bisher mag ich sie und hätte, bei mehr Auswahl, spezifischerer Anpassung und ohne die kleinen Kinderkrankheiten, gerne die 5 Sterner vergeben 😊

title: Tolle App mit Verbesserungspotenzial
body:
Tolle App!
Die Idee hinter Rise ist großartig – das Konzept ist richtig gut, das Design ist ansprechend, und die Funktionen motivieren.

Es gibt jedoch ein paar Punkte, die aus meiner Sicht unbedingt verbessert werden sollten:

1. Vorgeschlagene Zielwerte (z. B. Trainingsdauer) sind oft unrealistisch (z. B. 90 Min.) – bitte besser automatisch an den Alltag anpassen.
2. Feste Wochentage für Aufgaben (Training, joggen, etc.) sollten einmal zentral einstellbar sein.
3. Der Kalender startet aktuell am Sonntag – bitte Option für Montag als Wochenanfang anbieten.
4. Eine kurze Erklärung zur 66‑Tage‑Struktur wäre hilfreich, falls bestimmte Vorgaben bewusst so gewählt sind.
5. Die deutsche Version der App ist verständlich, aber an einigen Stellen sprachlich nicht ganz sauber (Grammatik/Wortwahl).

Falls Interesse des Entwicklers besteht, sende ich gern ein ausführlicheres Feedback zu diesen Punkten zu.

Ich freue mich schon auf die weitere Entwicklung der App!

title: Great concept, but too limited for advanced users
body:
The app has a great concept and helps in building healthy habits. The interface is user-friendly, and it offers a nice overview of daily tasks and goals. However, it feels quite limited when it comes to users who are already at a more advanced level.

For example, you can set a goal to read 30 pages per week, but if you read that amount (or more) daily, there’s no option to adjust the goal to match your actual habits. This lack of flexibility makes it hard to track real progress.

Additionally, the app’s evaluation system seems off — even though I consistently complete all my habits (working out, drinking water, reading, etc.), it still shows that I need improvement. It feels like I’m being compared to users who barely do anything, which can be demotivating.

It would be much more useful if the app allowed more customization so users could set goals that reflect their real routines and progress. I hope future updates bring more flexibility for users who are already consistent and want to keep improving.

body:

However, I wish there was more flexibility when it comes to the workout tracking. For example, not everyone can go running due to health reasons, but they might do other forms of exercise instead. Right now, there’s no way to mark a workout as “done” unless you do exactly what’s listed, which can be frustrating. I do work out regularly, just not by running – so it feels like my efforts aren’t being counted.

It would be amazing if we could swap or customize workouts (like switching from running to swimming or other activities) to better reflect our routines and still stay on track.

I hope this can be updated in the future – it would really improve the experience!

title: Good app that needs some polishing to reach its potential
body:
After some indecision I went ahead, payed and just jumped into this app.

My goal was to pick up healthier habits, a more organised structure to my day and to have fun facing the challenges.

After a week using the app I can see its pros and cons:

Pros:
- Great visuals & animations
- Solid concept
- Tasks that push you out of your comfort zone to better yourself
- Good selection of in-app tools

Cons:
-Static Tasks that ramp up too quickly 

For me the programme ramps up a bit too steeply by default. Going from not tracking water intake, not running or working out at all on upon stating to running and working out as much as the tasks demand I do by like week 3 seems too much too fast. 

I was hoping the app in standard mode would start me on smaller tasks and steadily build that mindset & capability up but each week but instead it just throws increased times at me as if I’ve not struggled and doesn’t seem to adapt my tasks when I’ve only partially completed them (an indicator that I’ve struggled and kinda need the next week NOT to be like 15 mins extra time and 1 day more frequently for seemingly no reason other than ‘deal with it’)

Those with long term issues like old knee injuries etc could benefit from a better thought out increase and task adaption and even varied tasks like another user put in their review.

In 66 days you might not be running 7km and working out for like 1.5 hours 4x a week this way but with better default increases to tasks it surely will see users build that strong well of resolve to do as much as that.

- Some awkward UI
The tasks ramping up wouldn’t be as much of an issue as you can customise the programme if not for the UI
Editing the programme can be can be clunky and awkward.
You seem to need to re-customise the programme after each weekly review and it doesn’t seem to apply the changes you made for the first day if thats when you made the changes. (Today I’m tasked with drinking 3L of water instead of the 2.5L a day I set, but the rest of the week is correct.

- Spelling & grammar
I could understand some issues in early versions but from what I payed for the year I really would expect words like ‘Strength’ to be spelled correctly and wouldn’t expect the sheer amount of spelling and grammar issues there are in the app.

Overall though a good app with some great potential once the issues are ironed out.

I would also love to see a restore default programme button in the mean time to remind me what the app intended for me and where I’m at.

But since I imagine the users are all here for growth I think it’s fair to give the developers a fair chance to grow the app too.

title: The App Has Been Significantly Improved; The Developer Really Listens to the Users!
body:
The first time I downloaded this app was on April 2025. I immediately subscribed to its annual plan because I saw good reviews… but then, I abandoned this app within a week because the in-app daily habit program was too rigid. 

Here’s the thing: in my case, I have always been an active person in terms of exercising/working out. I hit the gym 5 times a week where I do treadmill inclined walks and lift weights. What I wanted from this app back then was a way to improve my overall daily habit as in staying focused and get my mental health together. Yet, after inputting my current state, the app generated a program that asked me to run twice a week. This made no sense because I’ve been regularly exercising; adding running to it would cause me unnecessary fatigue. Not to mention that I hate looking like an undisciplined person who don’t tick off a mere running task in an app that I paid subscription for. I just don’t like skipping a task cz I’m a lil bit perfectionist. There was also no way to edit/customize the program as user myself at that time. 

I remember vaguely I wrote a complaint (as a feedback) to the developer at that time. Fast forward, I forgot about this app until yesterday. I decided to give it a try again only to find out that THIS APP HAS BEEN IMPROVED A LOT. WOW!

The user interface feels so light and easy to navigate than back then. I can also edit/customize the given tasks per day and even set the frequency myself. It also has embedded journal now to track our progress alongside the given tasks. Overall, I really love the current app!

With the current app’s enhanced recommendations and customization capability, this one is really helpful in building my better habits. Kudos to the developer!

Looking forward to this app’s next and continuous improvements!

title: Zajebiste
body: Jako gracz i fan anime, długo szukałem aplikacji, która by "zgamifikowała" moją produktywność w prawdziwym życiu i pomogła mi się trzymać planu... od małych rzeczy jak sprzątanie domu czy picie wody... po wielkie rzeczy jak praca nad biznesem. To najbardziej obiecująca aplikacja do dyscypliny i samorozwoju, jaką udało mi się znaleźć. Nie tylko to, ale deweloper naprawdę się stara i zbudował świetną społeczność na Discordzie, gdzie często gada z użytkownikami i jest otwarty na każdy feedback. Pomysł stojący za aplikacją mnie zainteresował, ale troska i uwaga, jaką właściciele jej poświęcają, sprawiły, że zostałem. To aplikacja stworzona nie przez jakąś korporację, ale przez chłopaków, którzy przeszli przez te same problemy co ja i wymyślili system, żeby poprawić swoje życie. Polecałbym tę aplikację każdemu, kto chce zrobić to samo.
author: TomcziWK

title: Świetny pomysł, ale potrzeba więcej elementów w stylu anime Solo Leveling
body: Life Reset to solidna aplikacja do budowania nawyków i samorozwoju, ale mogłaby być znacznie bardziej wciągająca, gdyby bardziej opierała się na stylu gryfikacji z Solo Leveling. Obecnie aplikacja całkiem nieźle śledzi postępy i sprawia, że samorozwój jest satysfakcjonujący, ale brakuje jej wizualnej transformacji i głębokich mechanik RPG, które sprawiłyby, że levelowanie w prawdziwym życiu byłoby tak ekscytujące jak levelowanie w grze. Wyobraź sobie, że wraz z postępem twoja postać fizycznie i mentalnie ewoluuje - zaczynasz jako słaba, niewytrenowana wersja siebie i stopniowo przemieniasz się w silniejszą, bystrzejszą, bardziej zdyscyplinowaną wersję opartą na twoich rzeczywistych postępach. Co prawda ostatnio część z tego już wprowadziliście. Kocham te uczucie gdy ukończenie treningu zwiększa mi statystyki siły, czytanie podnosi inteligencję, a zadania związane z dyscypliną odblokowują nowe bonusy. Gdyby Rise w pełni przyjął koncepcję Solo Leveling, mógłby być idealnym RPG-iem z prawdziwego życia. Głębsze drzewka umiejętności, questy, osiągnięcia i progresja postaci w czasie rzeczywistym sprawiłyby, że byłoby to znacznie bardziej angażujące i motywujące. Gryfikacja samorozwoju już teraz jest fajna, ale najlepszy sposób na utrzymanie motywacji to wizualne widzenie swoich postępów. Gdyby deweloperzy wprowadzili te zmiany, ta aplikacja mogłaby zmienić podejście do rozwoju osobistego. Obecnie to świetny start, ale mam nadzieję, że podniosą to na jeszcze wyższy poziom!

title: Yeah, You Have to Pay. Yeah, it’s Worth it.
body:
I (24M) got this app last year after being targeted hard with ads for the app. Needless to say, I’ve REALLY enjoyed it, and the developers are continuously improving the experience.

I’ve used other habit trackers before to no avail, but something about this one just clicks. If I had to describe why, it’s that the app “feels” like it’s on the journey with you. The UI is clean, and I love the art associated with the achievements, the tasks, and the motivation cards.

The task progression is pretty solid too. Where last year mandatory tasks like “wakeup early” were difficult to deal with if you’re on a swing shift like I am, this year it’s been customized to where you can simply achieve a minimum number of hours of rest. Super helpful update.

In future updates, I’d love to see a more “knowledge gaining” or “addiction breaking” or “workout focused” program development. There’s so many extra tasks in the portfolio that don’t get added to the docket unless I manually add them. And while I absolutely can do that, somehow it just takes the magic away, and in my brain makes it more of an “optional” task. If the app automatically built it into day 1 of a more focused program, my brain would perceive it as a much more important and critical task. Not just “an extra thing to do.”

Overall, I love Life Reset. I love watching my “levels” go up, and it’s a reminder that you need to level your self up daily just like you would for a character in a video game. Thank you developers!!!

title: All Visual No Depth
body: The app is beautiful. The gamification of a routine can be helpful to most to get started on the right path. Tasks are built on arbitrary numbers and preset schedules, nothing that actually adapts to you or your progress. Editing tasks or your schedule is limited. Simple week 1 tasks jump to insane asks by Week 5-6 that are so arbitrary that it’s clear no real thought or scientific backing goes into them. 90 minutes of lifting and 3+ miles run 6x a week? For someone who wasn’t working out to start? While possible for some, it invites injury or overworking the body unless you are already at that level, which you’re not if you’re using this app. There are other bugs and crashes that take away from the experience too. I’m just disappointed. A shallow app with a pretty face, it will help some start their journey after they fork over money, just to realize it’s unrealistic and they’ll have to look elsewhere to continue.

title: changed my life
body:
The Value of Life Reset: 66 Day Habit

In the field of personal development, many programs and methods are marketed as life-changing, but only a few provide a structure that is both practical and sustainable. Life Reset: 66 Day Habit distinguishes itself by focusing on the science of habit formation and presenting a framework that truly enables long-term transformation. For this reason, it deserves a five-star rating.

1. Scientific Foundation

The program is built on research from psychology and behavioral science that demonstrates it takes, on average, sixty-six days to form a new habit. Unlike vague promises of “instant change,” this timeframe is grounded in empirical findings. By aligning itself with science rather than shortcuts, the program builds credibility and sets realistic expectations.

2. Structured Guidance

Life Reset: 66 Day Habit does not simply advise readers to “be disciplined.” Instead, it provides a clear, day-by-day roadmap. Each day’s tasks build incrementally on the last, allowing participants to develop consistency without being overwhelmed. This progressive design makes the system approachable for people at all stages of self-improvement, from beginners to those seeking to refine existing habits.

3. Psychological Reinforcement

The program recognizes that motivation fluctuates. To address this, it incorporates strategies such as accountability check-ins, reflective prompts, and reward mechanisms. These elements strengthen perseverance during the difficult middle weeks, when many habit-building attempts usually fail. By weaving reinforcement into the daily practice, the program helps participants internalize habits more effectively than willpower alone.

4. Flexibility and Personalization

Another strength lies in its adaptability. Rather than prescribing a single universal habit, the program encourages individuals to choose the area of life most relevant to them—health, productivity, relationships, or emotional well-being. This personalization ensures that participants are not forced into rigid molds but can align the 66-day journey with their unique goals and values.

5. Tangible Results

The hallmark of any effective habit system is its outcomes. Users of Life Reset: 66 Day Habit consistently report measurable improvements: increased energy, more focused work routines, reduced stress, and enhanced self-confidence. Because the system emphasizes gradual reinforcement, the changes tend to endure long after the program is completed, making it more than a temporary motivational boost.

6. Long-Term Impact

Unlike many self-help approaches that fade once the initial enthusiasm wears off, this program establishes a replicable model. Participants not only form a single habit but also learn how to apply the same principles to future changes. In this way, Life Reset: 66 Day Habit functions as a lifelong tool rather than a one-time intervention.

⸻

Conclusion

Life Reset: 66 Day Habit is worthy of a five-star rating because it combines scientific rigor, practical structure, psychological reinforcement, and personal flexibility. By guiding individuals through the natural process of habit formation, it enables lasting improvements rather than temporary adjustments. More than a motivational slogan, it is a structured system that empowers people to reset their lives with confidence and clarity. For anyone serious about meaningful change, this program offers a reliable path forward.

The current approach, collecting extensive personal data without revealing the paywall until the end definitely raises concerns about data exploitation, akin to the practices of major tech companies such as Meta. Requiring a signature further amplifies these concerns and will compromise user trust. I request that my data be deleted immediately and strongly urge you to prioritize transparency by clearly communicating costs upfront.

AI supposedly sets goals for the different task with personalization based on a very basic survey they make you do in the beginning. Probably aimed mostly at people who haven’t subscribed yet. You can go in and edit goals individually and tell the app which days you want to but you have to change it by the week. If you go into week one on week one and add that you want to study a language for example, it will put goals for week one.

title: First review ever “Solo leveling esq”
body:
Never done a review before and I’ve never spent real money on a app before. Lots of these “self help” apps can be cliche or repetitive but this one is a breath of fresh air. 

Very clean art and the user interface separate this app from others, as well as the easy to use yet informative task and “level up” system. It really makes me take on the concept of “1 % better” each day or in this apps case 1 “point” better each day. I think it also helps that I just finished watching “Solo Leveling” which is a great anime and if you enjoyed watching that and you have any will to “level up” your life this will be the perfect app for you. 

This is all before the recent big update but it only seems to have gotten better from the update, it seems they genuinely care about making a better product for its user rather than trying to get a quick buck. I’m about 19 days in and loving it. Definitely would recommend if you’re looking for anything like this

title: Gimmicky money grab
body:
It starts off with a series of questions “How much do you work out, study, drink water? Etc.” I already have a good life and just like to try things like this for fun. I workout 5-6 hours a week, have a healthy diet & no bad habits. After answering all the questions it tells me I have ~40% more bad habits than the average guy my age. Literally impossible but lol okay? I’m convinced it says that for everyone no matter what you answer because they’re trying to convince you to give them money. Then it spends another 5 minutes telling you how this app will change your life and make all your problems go away etc. And the “program” it created for me actually had me doing LESS to better my life lol. Then after wasting your time answering questions they don’t actually use for anything they hit you with the “$12.99/month discount!”. 

You’re better off writing yourself a schedule and looking to other sources for motivation. This company is just trying to ride off the coat tails of Solo Leveling. If you want something fun like that you’re better off downloading the Level-Up app. At least it’s free and doesn’t try to pretend to be something it’s not. The only reason this isn’t getting one star is because maybe I could see this app being useful if you’re at rock bottom and need any way possible to get out.

title: Great Concept, But Needs More Solo Leveling Elements
body: Rise: Life Reset in 66 Days is a solid app for habit-building and self-improvement, but it could be so much more immersive if it leaned further into the Solo Leveling style of gamification. Right now, the app does a decent job of tracking progress and making self-improvement feel rewarding, but it lacks the visual transformation and deep RPG mechanics that would make leveling up in real life feel as exciting as leveling up in a game. Imagine if, as you progressed, your character physically and mentally evolved—starting as a weak, untrained version of yourself and gradually transforming into a stronger, sharper, more disciplined version based on your real-life progress. Completing workouts should increase strength stats, reading should boost intelligence, and discipline-related tasks should unlock new “abilities” or perks. If Rise fully embraced the Solo Leveling concept, it could be the ultimate real-life RPG. Deeper skill trees, quests, achievements, and real-time character progression would make it way more engaging and motivating. Gamifying self-improvement is already fun, but the best way to stay motivated is to see your progress visually. If the developers make these changes, this app could become a game-changer for personal growth. Right now, it’s a great start, but I hope they push it to the next level!
